correctness.rationale: Analytic product identity gives normalized signed moments; coefficient recurrence has one negative atom and all remaining nonconstant coefficients positive for pa<b<p²a. Dividing every order-m difference by the positive k=1 contribution shows the worst tail is n=0. The increasing R_m has R_1<1 and diverges, giving a unique threshold. Uniform positive q-product bounds give c_k/(-c1) comparable to epsilon*a^(k-2); the geometric saddle S_m comparable to m^(-beta) yields R_m comparable to epsilon*exp(Lm)*m^(-beta), and inversion supplies the stated log/loglog formula. All comparisons use constants uniform for small epsilon. Diagnostics are finite only.

value.rationale: The original geometric weighted-shift literature identifies a complete-hyperexpansivity ray but not the stability depth of finitely many inequalities just beyond it. The theorem quantifies the maximal order of valid inequalities for all tail vectors and identifies a nontrivial extra log-log layer; this explains why finite-order experiments can falsely suggest complete hyperexpansivity near the boundary. Continuous two-parameter validity and exact order testing make it more than an arbitrary finite example.
